def-ewald-causal-cardinal-spline-window:
## Definition

For $P=1$ set $W_1(u)=\mathbf 1_{[0,1]}(u)$, including both endpoints. For an
integer $P\ge2$, define the causal order-$P$ window by
$$W_P(u)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac1{(P-1)!}\sum_{j=0}^{P}(-1)^j\binom Pj(u-j)_+^{P-1},&0\le u\le P,\\0,&u<0\text{ or }u>P.\end{cases}$$
Here $s_+=\max(s,0)$, $m!$ is the factorial of the nonnegative integer $m$
with $0!=1$, and for integers $0\le j\le P$,
$\binom Pj=P!/(j!(P-j)!)$. Convolution means the integral operation
$$(f*g)(u)=\int_{\mathbb R}f(u-s)g(s)\,ds,$$
when the integrand is measurable and integrable, as in
[[def-convolution-of-two-functions-on-rn]]. The displayed formula is finite at
every $u$ and directly defines $W_P$ to vanish outside $[0,P]$; the local
alias lemma proves that it agrees with the $P$-fold convolution of $W_1$ and
establishes the resulting integral, positivity, partition, Fourier-transform,
and derivative identities.
def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-sou:
## Definition

Let $A\in GL_3(\mathbb R)$, let $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$, let
$V=|\det A|$, and let $\mathbb T_A=\mathbb R^3/\Lambda$. These are the
full-rank lattice and covolume conventions of
[[def-full-rank-lattice-covolume-and-dual-lattice]]. The reciprocal lattice is
$\Lambda^*=A^{-T}\mathbb Z^3$. For $k\in\mathbb Z^3$ write
$$\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k,\qquad e_k(x)=e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}.$$
Thus $e_k$ is a character of $\mathbb T_A$; the ordinary Fourier frequency is
$A^{-T}k$, while $\kappa_k$ is the angular physical frequency.

A finite point-source configuration consists of an integer $n\ge0$, points
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb T_A$ that are pairwise distinct when $n>1$, and
real charges $q_1,\ldots,q_n$. It is **neutral** when
$\sum_{i=1}^n q_i=0$. For a smooth periodic test function $\varphi$, the
point-source distribution is the linear functional
$$\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^nq_i\varphi(x_i).$$
Here smooth means that the periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$ has continuous
derivatives of every order, and the test-function topology is generated by the
seminorms $\max_{x\in A[0,1]^3}|\partial^\beta\varphi(x)|$ over all derivative
multi-indices $\beta$. A periodic distribution is a continuous complex-linear
functional for this topology. Its distributional Laplacian is defined by
$\langle-\Delta u,\varphi\rangle=\langle u,-\Delta\varphi\rangle$.

For a smooth periodic $\varphi$, its Fourier coefficient is
$$\widehat\varphi(k)=\frac1V\int_{A(0,1]^3}\varphi(x)e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x}\,dx.$$
The source coefficient is
$$\widehat\rho(k)=\frac1V\sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i};$$
in particular, neutral data have $\widehat\rho(0)=0$. For a periodic
distribution $u$, define $\widehat u(k)=V^{-1}\langle u,e_{-k}\rangle$. The
**mean-zero periodic Poisson solution** is a periodic distribution $u$ satisfying
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$ and $\widehat u(0)=0$. This definition fixes the
zero-mode convention; no nonneutral periodic solution is implicit.

The Coulomb energy convention is the half-sum of each source charge times the
regular part of its potential, after subtracting its own singular term
$q_i/|x-x_i|$. The resulting finite part is called the **renormalized
self-energy convention**. Its Ewald formula is established in this development.
lem-ewald-screened-coulomb-kernel-and-se:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For $\alpha>0$, define
$$g_\alpha(x)=\frac{\alpha^3}{\pi^{3/2}}e^{-\alpha^2|x|^2},\quad \operatorname{erf}(s)=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}\int_0^s e^{-t^2}\,dt,\quad \operatorname{erfc}(s)=1-\operatorname{erf}(s).$$
Here $\Delta=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}^2$, $\delta_0$ is the distribution
$\langle\delta_0,\varphi\rangle=\varphi(0)$, and a test function is a smooth
compactly supported function $\varphi$.
For $r=|x|>0$ put $\phi_\ell(r)=\operatorname{erf}(\alpha r)/r$ and
$\phi_s(r)=\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r)/r$. Then $\phi_\ell$ extends
continuously to $r=0$, $-\Delta\phi_\ell=4\pi g_\alpha$ distributionally on
$\mathbb R^3$, and $-\Delta\phi_s=4\pi\delta_0-4\pi g_\alpha$. Moreover,
for every $s\ge0$,
$$\operatorname{erfc}(s)=\frac2{\sqrt\pi}\int_s^\infty e^{-t^2}\,dt,$$
$$\phi_s(r)=\frac1r-\frac{2\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}+O(r^2)\quad(r\downarrow0),$$
and for every $r>0$,
$$0\le\phi_s(r)\le\frac{e^{-\alpha^2r^2}}{\sqrt\pi\alpha r^2},\qquad |\phi_s'(r)|\le\frac{2\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\frac{e^{-\alpha^2r^2}}r+ \frac{e^{-\alpha^2r^2}}{\sqrt\pi\alpha r^3}.$$
def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model:
## Definition

Fix neutral point-source data $(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], an Ewald parameter
$\alpha>0$, integers $M_1,M_2,M_3\ge1$, an assignment order $P\ge2$, and write
$N_g=M_1M_2M_3$. Let $\mathcal G=\prod_{r=1}^3\{0,\ldots,M_r-1\}$ and take
$W_P$ from [[def-ewald-causal-cardinal-spline-window]]. Define the periodic
causal assignment weights, for $t\in[0,1)^3$ and $\ell\in\mathcal G$, by
$$w_\ell(t)=\prod_{r=1}^3\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z} W_P(M_rt_r-\ell_r-jM_r).$$
The sums are finite because $W_P$ is supported on $[0,P]$. They collect every
support index into its grid residue; if $P>M_r$, distinct support indices that
wrap to the same residue are added. The spread grid is
$$g_\ell=\sum_{i=1}^n q_iw_\ell(t_i),\qquad t_i=A^{-1}x_i\pmod{\mathbb Z^3}.$$

Use the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT convention
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_{r=1}^3k_r\ell_r/M_r},$$
which is the product transform of
[[def-unitary-discrete-fourier-transform-on-z-mod-n]]. Signed frequency
representatives are chosen before evaluating windows. A retained set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ is finite, symmetric under
$k\mapsto-k$, injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$, and satisfies
$|k_r|<M_r/2$ for each coordinate. In particular, even-grid Nyquist modes are
not silently retained.

For $u\in\mathbb R$, put $\operatorname{sinc}(u)=\sin(u)/u$ when $u\ne0$ and
$\operatorname{sinc}(0)=1$. Define
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r} \operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P.$$
Only modes with $D(k)\ne0$ are admissible for division. A computed
implementation must first certify a strictly positive lower bound for
$|D(k)|$; otherwise it returns `denominator-inconclusive` without dividing.
For $k\in\mathcal K$, define
$$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t},\quad b_k(t)=\frac{\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t) e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}}{\overline{D(k)}},\quad \rho_k=\sum_iq_i a_k(t_i),\quad z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}}.$$
The denominator is the complex conjugate of the printed window multiplier; this
sign is part of the definition. Set
$$c_k=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2} e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}.$$
The exact retained reciprocal energy is
$$E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2,$$
and the mesh reciprocal energy is
$$E_M=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2.$$

Let $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ be the declared physical mesh derivative: it is
$\nabla_xb_k(t)=A^{-T}\nabla_tb_k(t)$ wherever the classical derivative
exists. A grid knot is a point with $M_rt_r\in\mathbb Z$ for some coordinate
$r$. At a $P=2$ knot, take the one-sided vector limits from all adjacent open
mesh boxes. Define $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ to be any selected one-sided limit or the
arithmetic average of all those limits. This is a procedure value and does not
assert that the classical derivative exists there. The
energy-gradient mesh force is
$$F_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\overline{z_k}\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\right).$$
Define the diagonal mesh-self correction and corrected reciprocal energy by
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k (|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E_M^{\mathrm{corr}}=E_M-C_M.$$
Whether the declared force is the derivative of this corrected energy, and the
error bound it satisfies, are proved separately.
lem-ewald-gaussian-poisson-periodization:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and use the full-rank cell and angular frequencies of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Here $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$
denotes the Schwartz space of smooth functions whose derivatives decay faster
than every inverse polynomial. For $\alpha>0$ let
$$g_\alpha(x)=\frac{\alpha^3}{\pi^{3/2}}e^{-\alpha^2|x|^2}.$$
For every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the two series below converge absolutely, locally
uniformly in $x$, and
$$\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}g_\alpha(x+\lambda)= \frac1V\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3} e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}.$$
The lattice Poisson theorem is applied only to this Schwartz Gaussian; it is not
applied to a compactly supported or finite-smoothness assignment window.
lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-co:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. For an invertible real $3\times3$ matrix $B$, put
$\Gamma=B\mathbb Z^3$ and
$$C_B=\bigl(2\|B^{-1}\|_2(1+\sqrt3\|B\|_2)+1\bigr)^3.$$
Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean operator norm. Uniformly over every
translate $y+\Gamma$ and every integer shell $m\ge0$,
$$\#\{z\in y+\Gamma:m\le|z|<m+1\}\le C_B(m+1)^3.$$

For $\beta>0$, any integer $p\ge0$, and integer $M\ge0$, set
$$T_p(\beta,M)=\sum_{m=M}^{\infty}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2}.$$
For any integer $J\ge M$ satisfying $2\beta J(J+1)\ge p$, define
$$I_0(J,\beta)=\frac{\sqrt\pi}{2\sqrt\beta}\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt\beta J),\quad I_1(J,\beta)=\frac{e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta},$$
and recursively for $2\le s\le p$,
$$I_s(J,\beta)=\frac{J^{s-1}e^{-\beta J^2}}{2\beta} +\frac{s-1}{2\beta}I_{s-2}(J,\beta).$$
Then the finite controller
$$U_p(\beta,M,J)=\sum_{m=M}^{J}(m+1)^p e^{-\beta m^2} +\sum_{s=0}^{p}\binom ps I_s(J,\beta)$$
satisfies $T_p(\beta,M)\le U_p(\beta,M,J)$. Such a $J$ exists for every
$\beta>0$, $M\ge0$, and integer $p\ge0$.
lem-ewald-smooth-torus-fourier-pairing:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $A\in GL_3(\mathbb R)$, $V=|\det A|$,
$\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$, $\kappa_k=2\pi A^{-T}k$, and let $\varphi$ be a smooth
$\Lambda$-periodic function. With the Fourier coefficients of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], for every derivative
order $q\ge0$,
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}|\kappa_k|^q|\widehat\varphi(k)|<\infty.$$
Consequently the Fourier series of $\varphi$ and every differentiated series
converge uniformly to $\varphi$ and its corresponding derivatives. More
generally, if a coefficient sequence satisfies
$|a_k|\le C(1+|\kappa_k|)^s$ for some $C<\infty$ and $s\ge0$, then
$$T_a(\varphi):=V\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}a_k\widehat\varphi(-k)$$
converges absolutely and defines a continuous periodic distribution. A
periodic distribution is determined by its Fourier coefficients.
lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-norma:
## Statement

Use the periodic cardinal-assignment model of
[[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], with integers $M_r\ge1$, order
$P\ge2$, grid size $N_g=\prod_rM_r$, a retained signed mode $k$ satisfying
$|k_r|<M_r/2$, and $D(k)\ne0$. Put $u_r=k_r/M_r$,
$a_k(t)=e^{-2\pi i k\cdot t}$, and
$$r_{k,n}=\prod_{r=1}^3 \frac{\overline{D_r(k_r+n_rM_r)}}{\overline{D_r(k_r)}},\qquad D_r(m)=e^{-\pi iPm/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi m/M_r)^P.$$
Then the single-particle assignment factor and the spread-grid coefficient obey
the absolutely convergent identities
$$b_k(t)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}a_{k+n\odot M}(t),\qquad z_k=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M},$$
where $(n\odot M)_r=n_rM_r$ and
$\rho_j=\sum_iq_i e^{-2\pi i j\cdot t_i}$. In particular
$$z_k-\rho_k=\sum_{n\ne0}r_{k,n}\rho_{k+n\odot M}.$$
The mesh coefficient also has the exact finite representation
$z_k=\sum_iq_i b_k(t_i)$, so no cell-volume or grid-size factor remains after
the displayed $\sqrt{N_g}$ conversion. The alias bound below uses only the Fourier series of
the compact spline; the lattice Poisson theorem is not applied to that spline.

For $u_r\ne0$ define
$$a_r(P,u_r)=\sum_{m\ne0}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P, \qquad a_r(P,0)=0,\qquad A_k=\prod_{r=1}^3(1+a_r(P,u_r))-1.$$
Then $|b_k(t)-a_k(t)|\le A_k$, $|b_k(t)|\le1+A_k$, and
$|z_k-\rho_k|\le Q A_k$ for $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$. For $J\ge1$ and
$0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r(P,u_r)\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\sum_{m=1}^\infty m^{-P},\qquad \sum_{|m|>J}\left|\frac{u_r}{u_r+m}\right|^P\le 2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\frac{J^{1-P}}{P-1}.$$
Thus every alias controller has a finite p-series remainder bound.
The periodic assignment also satisfies $\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(t)=1$,
so the spread-grid zero mode is $\sum_{\ell}g_\ell=\sum_iq_i=0$ for neutral data.
thm-ewald-neutral-periodic-poisson-green:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and a neutral finite point-source configuration on the
cell $A\mathbb Z^3$ of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Put
$$\widehat u(0)=0,\qquad \widehat u(k)=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2} \sum_{i=1}^nq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i}\quad(k\ne0).$$
The polynomially bounded sequence $\widehat u(k)$ defines a periodic
distribution $u$ by Fourier pairing. It is the unique mean-zero periodic
distribution satisfying $-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$.
lem-ewald-pme-derivative-window-alias-bo:
## Statement

Use the data and aliases of
[[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]]. Write
$h_r(0)=1$ and, for $u_r=k_r/M_r\ne0$,
$h_r(n)=|u_r/(u_r+n)|^P$ for $n\ne0$; when $u_r=0$, set $h_r(n)=0$ for
$n\ne0$. Put
$$a_r=\sum_{n\ne0}h_r(n).$$
For $P\ge3$, define
$$v_r=\sum_{n\ne0}|k_r+nM_r|h_r(n),\qquad J_{k,r}=(|k_r|+v_r)\prod_{s\ne r}(1+a_s)-|k_r|,$$
and
$$B_k=2\pi\|A^{-T}\|_2\left(\sum_{r=1}^3J_{k,r}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
For $P\ge3$ the physical derivative alias error satisfies
$$\|\nabla_xb_k(t)-\nabla_xa_k(t)\|_2\le B_k.$$
Each series has a finite p-series controller: for $0<|u_r|<1/2$,
$$a_r\le2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\zeta(P),\qquad v_r\le2M_r\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^{P-1}}\zeta(P-1),$$
where $\zeta(s)=\sum_{m\ge1}m^{-s}$ for $s>1$. After summing exactly over
$1\le|n|\le J_0$, the respective omitted tails are at most
$$2\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^P}\frac{J_0^{1-P}}{P-1},\qquad 2M_r\frac{|u_r|^P}{(1-|u_r|)^{P-1}}\frac{J_0^{2-P}}{P-2}.$$

For the approved $P=2$ case, the absolute derivative p-series above diverges
when $u_r\ne0$. Instead use the finite derivative of the local piecewise
window sum. At every open mesh box and each one-sided knot limit, put
$$C_{k,r}=\frac{2M_r}{|D(k)|}+2\pi|k_r|,\qquad B_k=\|A^{-T}\|_2\left(\sum_{r=1}^3C_{k,r}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
This is a computable finite bound for the same physical derivative error. At a
grid knot, use the declared $\mathfrak d_k(t)$ branch from
[[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]]: it is a selected one-sided value
or their average and obeys the bound, but is not asserted to be a classical
derivative there. Thus for the full $P\ge2$ range the bound is on
$\mathfrak d_k(t)-\nabla_xa_k(t)$, with $\mathfrak d_k=\nabla_xb_k$ wherever
the classical derivative exists.
thm-ewald-alpha-independent-energy-and-p:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite point-source data
$(A,V,\Lambda,\kappa_k,(x_i,q_i)_{i=1}^n)$ from
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]], with pairwise distinct
source positions in $\mathbb T_A$. For $\alpha>0$ put
$$\sigma_k=\sum_iq_i e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i},\qquad c_k(\alpha)=\frac{4\pi}{V|\kappa_k|^2}e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}\quad(k\ne0).$$
For every off-source point $x\notin\bigcup_i(x_i+\Lambda)$, the absolutely
convergent Ewald potential
$$U_\alpha(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda} \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x-x_i+\lambda|)}{|x-x_i+\lambda|} +\frac{4\pi}{V}\sum_{k\ne0}\frac{e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{|\kappa_k|^2} \sigma_k e^{i\kappa_k\cdot x}$$
is the off-source representative of the unique mean-zero periodic solution of
$-\Delta u=4\pi\rho$. Hence it is independent of $\alpha$.

Define the regular part at $x_i$ by
$$\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha= \lim_{x\to x_i}\left(U_\alpha(x)-\frac{q_i}{|x-x_i|}\right).$$
The limit exists, is independent of $\alpha$, and the renormalized energy is
$$E=\frac12\sum_iq_i\operatorname{FP}_{x_i}U_\alpha =\frac12\sum_i\sum_{(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)}q_iq_j \frac{\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)} {|x_i-x_j+\lambda|} +\frac12\sum_{k\ne0}c_k(\alpha)|\sigma_k|^2 -\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2.$$
The prime-exclusion written as $(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0)$ omits only each particle's
own zero-image singularity.
thm-ewald-pme-reciprocal-energy-force-er:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and neutral finite source data on the cell $A\mathbb Z^3$
from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix $\alpha>0$,
integers $M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric set
$\mathcal K\subset\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}$ whose signed representatives are
injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and satisfy $|k_r|<M_r/2$. Require $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$, and let $c_k=4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}/(V|\kappa_k|^2)$ be the positive Ewald coefficient. Use the assignment factors $a_k,b_k,\rho_k,z_k$ of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]], and put $Q=\sum_j|q_j|$.

For a query point $x$ write $t=A^{-1}x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^3$ and define the retained exact and mesh reciprocal potentials by
$$U_{\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\rho_k\overline{a_k(t)}),\qquad U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(z_k\overline{b_k(t)}).$$
Define $E_{\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|\rho_k|^2$ and $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$. For each mode let $A_k$ be the source-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-spline-alias-and-dft-normalization]], and let $B_k$ be the derivative-alias controller in [[lem-ewald-pme-derivative-window-alias-bound]].

Let a complex-vector derivative/gather value $d_k(t)$ satisfy $\|d_k(t)-\mathfrak d_k(t)\|_2\le H_k$ for a stated $H_k\ge0$, where $\mathfrak d_k$ is the declared derivative branch of [[def-ewald-pme-cardinal-assignment-model]] and $\nabla_x=A^{-T}\nabla_t$. The uncorrected mesh and exact reciprocal forces are
$$F^d_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{z_k}d_k(t_i)),\qquad F_{\mathcal K,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\rho_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
Then for every query point $x$,
$$|U_{M,\mathcal K}(x)-U_{\mathcal K}(x)|\le Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),\qquad |E_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k),$$
and for every particle $i$,
$$\|F^d_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k\bigr].$$

For the declared energy-gradient gather $d_k=\mathfrak d_k$ (so $H_k=0$), the mesh force is $-\nabla_{x_i}E_{M,\mathcal K}$ wherever the classical derivative exists. This holds everywhere for $P\ge3$ and off the assignment knots for $P=2$; at a $P=2$ knot the selected one-sided derivative or its average is a procedure value, with the same bound but without a differentiability claim.

The optional diagonal self correction is
$$C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k(|b_k(t_i)|^2-1),\qquad E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}=E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M.$$
It satisfies
$$|E^{\rm corr}_{M,\mathcal K}-E_{\mathcal K}|\le\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k).$$
In the energy-gradient branch its exactly differentiated force is
$$F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}=-q_i\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\operatorname{Re}\bigl(\overline{z_k-q_ib_k(t_i)}\,\mathfrak d_k(t_i)\bigr),$$
and
$$\|F^{\rm corr}_{M,i}-F_{\mathcal K,i}\|_2\le |q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k\bigl[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k\bigr].$$
The corrected force is the classical gradient in the same differentiable cases; at a $P=2$ knot it is only the declared branch value. No pointwise error estimate here replaces an RMS estimate, and no claim is made that a different spectral differentiation rule is the gradient of the mesh energy.
thm-ewald-real-reciprocal-cutoff-error-b:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the neutral finite configuration and full-rank cell of
[[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Let
$Q=\sum_i|q_i|$, choose real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K\ge1$, and put
$M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$, $M_K=\lfloor K\rfloor$. Let $C_R=C_A$ be the shell
constant for $\Lambda=A\mathbb Z^3$ and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ the shell constant
for the angular reciprocal lattice. For the real-space cutoff, retain all
$(i,j,\lambda)$ with $|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R$ except $(i,i,0)$. For the
reciprocal cutoff, retain all $k\ne0$ with $|\kappa_k|\le K$. Use the
$T_3(\beta,M)$ controller of
[[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Then the omitted tails
in the exact Ewald potential, energy, and particle force satisfy
$$B_R^U=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),\qquad B_R^E=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
$$B_R^{F,i}=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1}) T_3(\alpha^2,M_R),$$
and
$$B_K^U=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),\qquad B_K^E=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K),$$
$$B_K^{F,i}=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V} T_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K).$$
For a certified finite value, replace each $T_3$ by the corresponding finite
upper controller $U_3$. The real force is evaluated only away from collisions;
no field bound is asserted at a point source.

The exact force is the negative gradient of the renormalized energy. With
$r_{ij\lambda}=|x_i-x_j+\lambda|$ and $a_k(t_i)=e^{-i\kappa_k\cdot x_i}$,
it is
$$F_i=-q_i\sum_{j=1}^n\sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda}'q_j\phi_s'(r_{ij\lambda})\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{r_{ij\lambda}}-q_i\sum_{k\ne0}c_k\operatorname{Re}(\overline{\sigma_k}\nabla_xa_k(t_i)).$$
The prime excludes only $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$; the absolutely convergent
reciprocal sum is real by pairing $k$ and $-k$.
thm-ewald-total-pme-error-certificate:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and a neutral finite point-source configuration on
$A\mathbb Z^3$ from [[def-ewald-three-dimensional-periodic-source-data]]. Fix
$\alpha>0$, real and reciprocal cutoffs $R,K_c\ge1$, a mesh with integers
$M_r\ge1$ and order $P\ge2$, and a finite symmetric retained set
$\mathcal K\subseteq\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|\kappa_k|\le K_c\}$
that is injective modulo $(M_1,M_2,M_3)$ and has $|k_r|<M_r/2$ and $D(k)\ne0$
for every $k\in\mathcal K$. Put $Q=\sum_i|q_i|$ and let
$$\mathcal B_{K_c}=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|\kappa_k|\le K_c\},\qquad \mathcal M_{K_c}=\mathcal B_{K_c}\setminus\mathcal K.$$
This in-ball omitted set is finite. Write $M_R=\lfloor R\rfloor$,
$M_K=\lfloor K_c\rfloor$, $C_R=C_A$, and $C_K=C_{2\pi A^{-T}}$ for the shell
constants in [[lem-ewald-lattice-shell-gaussian-tail-controllers]]. Choose
integers $J_R\ge M_R$, $J_K\ge M_K$ such that
$2\alpha^2J_R(J_R+1)\ge3$ and
$\frac{1}{2\alpha^2}J_K(J_K+1)\ge3$. Let $U_3(\beta,M,J)$ be that supplier's
finite upper controller for $\sum_{m=M}^\infty(m+1)^3e^{-\beta m^2}$, and put
$$\begin{aligned} \overline B_R^U&=\frac{QC_R}{\sqrt\pi\alpha}U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),& \overline B_R^E&=\frac{Q^2C_R}{2\sqrt\pi\alpha}U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),& \overline B_R^{F,i}&=\frac{|q_i|QC_R}{\sqrt\pi}(2\alpha+\alpha^{-1})U_3(\alpha^2,M_R,J_R),\\ \overline B_K^U&=\frac{4\pi QC_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K),& \overline B_K^E&=\frac{2\pi Q^2C_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K),& \overline B_K^{F,i}&=\frac{4\pi|q_i|QC_K}{V}U_3((4\alpha^2)^{-1},M_K,J_K). \end{aligned}$$

For $\phi_s(r)=\operatorname{erfc}(\alpha r)/r$, define the finite real-space
potential at an off-source point by
$$S_R(x)=\sum_iq_i\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\|x-x_i+\lambda|\le R}}\phi_s(|x-x_i+\lambda|),$$
and the finite real energy by
$$E_R=\frac12\sum_i\sum_j\sum_{\substack{\lambda\in\Lambda\\|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R}}'q_iq_j\phi_s(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|),$$
where the prime omits exactly $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$. Let
$$F_{R,i}=-q_i\sum_{\substack{1\le j\le n,\ \lambda\in\Lambda\\(j,\lambda)\ne(i,0),\,|x_i-x_j+\lambda|\le R}}q_j\,\phi_s'(|x_i-x_j+\lambda|)\frac{x_i-x_j+\lambda}{|x_i-x_j+\lambda|}.$$
The cutoff index set is held fixed in this force sum; the cutoff indicator is
not differentiated. Set
$$\widetilde U(x)=S_R(x)+U_{M,\mathcal K}(x),$$
$$\widetilde E^\chi=E_R+E_{M,\mathcal K}^\chi-\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt\pi}\sum_iq_i^2,\qquad \widetilde F_i^\chi=F_{R,i}+F_{M,i}^\chi,$$
where $\chi=\mathrm{uncorr}$ uses the uncorrected energy and force of
[[thm-ewald-pme-reciprocal-energy-force-error-bound]], and $\chi=\mathrm{corr}$ uses
its optional diagonal self-corrected branch. For the uncorrected branch suppose
the derivative/gather residuals are $H_k$; the corrected branch uses the
energy-gradient gather, so $H_k=0$.

Suppose the computed finite outputs $\widehat U(x),\widehat E^\chi,\widehat
F_i^\chi$ have certified arithmetic radii $\varepsilon_U,\varepsilon_E,
\varepsilon_{F,i}\ge0$ relative to $\widetilde U,\widetilde E^\chi,
\widetilde F_i^\chi$, respectively. Define
$$\begin{aligned} \eta_U={}&\overline B_R^U+\overline B_K^U+Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_U,\\ \eta_E^{\mathrm{uncorr}}={}&\overline B_R^E+\overline B_K^E+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_E,\\ \eta_E^{\mathrm{corr}}={}&\overline B_R^E+\overline B_K^E+\frac{Q^2}{2}\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m+\frac{Q^2-\sum_iq_i^2}{2}\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_kA_k(2+A_k)+\varepsilon_E,\\ \eta_{F,i}^{\mathrm{uncorr}}={}&\overline B_R^{F,i}+\overline B_K^{F,i}+|q_i|Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m|\kappa_m|+|q_i|Q\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k+(1+A_k)H_k]+\varepsilon_{F,i},\\ \eta_{F,i}^{\mathrm{corr}}={}&\overline B_R^{F,i}+\overline B_K^{F,i}+|q_i|Q\sum_{m\in\mathcal M_{K_c}}c_m|\kappa_m|+|q_i|(Q-|q_i|)\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k[|\kappa_k|A_k+(1+A_k)B_k]+\varepsilon_{F,i}. \end{aligned}$$
Then, for every off-source $x$ and each particle $i$,
$$|\widehat U(x)-U_\alpha(x)|\le\eta_U,\qquad |\widehat E^\chi-E|\le\eta_E^\chi,\qquad \|\widehat F_i^\chi-F_i\|_2\le\eta_{F,i}^\chi.$$
Here $U_\alpha,E,F_i$ are the exact mean-zero periodic Ewald potential,
renormalized energy, and particle force. The finite omitted-mode sums
$\mathcal M_{K_c}$ explicitly charge every mode in the radial ball that the
mesh did not retain, including Nyquist modes. Missing arithmetic radii do not
produce a certificate; no RMS estimate is substituted for these deterministic
bounds.
alg-ewald-certified-particle-mesh-evalua:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Inputs are a full-rank real cell matrix $A$, a finite
neutral configuration of pairwise-distinct torus positions $x_i$ and real
charges $q_i$, an Ewald parameter $\alpha>0$, cutoffs $R,K_c\ge1$, integers
$M_r\ge1$, an order $P\ge2$, a mesh-self-correction flag, an optional off-source
query point $x$, and requested nonnegative tolerances for potential, energy,
and each force. The input representation must provide certified enclosures for
the cell, positions, charges, cutoffs, and elementary functions, or an explicit
outward-enclosure oracle for every finite arithmetic node. If neutrality,
distinctness, full rank, or a required input enclosure cannot be certified,
return `invalid-input`; if $\sum_iq_i\ne0$ is certified, return `nonneutral`;
if a query point is a source image, return `collision` for that potential query.

1. Form the finite radial set $\mathcal B_{K_c}=\{k\in\mathbb Z^3\setminus\{0\}:|2\pi A^{-T}k|\le K_c\}$. Enumerate it inside the certified integer box implied by $|k|\le\|A^T\|_2K_c/(2\pi)$. Retain the modes satisfying $|k_r|<M_r/2$ for all coordinates and store their signed representatives in $\mathcal K$. This set is finite, symmetric and injective modulo the mesh. Every excluded mode in $\mathcal B_{K_c}$ is kept in the finite omitted-mode ledger $\mathcal M_{K_c}=\mathcal B_{K_c}\setminus\mathcal K$; it is never assigned zero error.

2. For each particle write $t_i=A^{-1}x_i$ modulo $\mathbb Z^3$. Compute the periodic assignment
$$w_\ell(t_i)=\prod_{r=1}^3\sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}W_P(M_rt_{i,r}-\ell_r-jM_r),\qquad g_\ell=\sum_iq_iw_\ell(t_i).$$
For each coordinate sum every integer translate whose argument lies in $[0,P]$. Accumulate all terms that wrap to the same residue; when $P>M_r$, do not merge them by dropping duplicate contributions. The support is the causal predecessor support of the window, not an unspecified symmetric nearest-node rule.

3. Apply the negative-sign unitary tensor DFT
$$\widehat g_M(k)=N_g^{-1/2}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}g_\ell e^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r},\qquad N_g=M_1M_2M_3,$$
by applying the published one-dimensional computed DFT procedure along each coordinate fiber and dividing that coordinate transform by $\sqrt{M_r}$. The required mathematical output convention is the unitary transform; each one-dimensional procedure itself returns the unnormalised DFT. The correctness-and-cost supplier proves the formal exact-constant transform identity and arithmetic-operation count. It is not used as a floating-point error bound; only the supplied outward node enclosures certify arithmetic values. If a transform subcall returns a failure status, return `transform-inconclusive`.

4. For each retained $k$, form the window multiplier
$$D(k)=\prod_{r=1}^3e^{-\pi iPk_r/M_r}\operatorname{sinc}(\pi k_r/M_r)^P$$
and obtain an outward lower bound for $|D(k)|$. If any lower bound is nonpositive, return `denominator-inconclusive` without division. Otherwise set
$$z_k=\frac{\sqrt{N_g}\,\widehat g_M(k)}{\overline{D(k)}},\qquad c_k=\frac{4\pi e^{-|\kappa_k|^2/(4\alpha^2)}}{V|\kappa_k|^2}.$$
Use the conjugated denominator forced by the negative-sign DFT and the causal window. The signed mode representative is used in every window factor; residues are used only as storage indices.

5. Form mode arrays on the full mesh-frequency grid, placing retained signed modes in their unique residues and setting all other entries to zero. Set $v^U_k=c_kz_k/D(k)$ on $\mathcal K$. Apply the same per-coordinate $M_r^{-1/2}$ normalization as in Step 3 to the negative-sign tensor DFT of $\overline{v^U}$, conjugate the output, and multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$; the exact result is $u_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}v^U_ke^{2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$. The off-source mesh potential is $\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}w_\ell(A^{-1}x)u_\ell$. For forces set $v^F_k=c_k\overline{z_k}/\overline{D(k)}$ on $\mathcal K$, zero elsewhere, and apply the same per-coordinate normalization to its negative-sign tensor DFT, then multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$ to form $\lambda_\ell=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}v^F_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_r\ell_r/M_r}$. Then $F_{M,i}=-q_i\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal G}\lambda_\ell\nabla_xw_\ell(t_i)$, gathering only the at most $P^3$ support contributions per particle. At a $P=2$ knot, compute every weight derivative from the same selected adjacent mesh box, or average them over all adjacent boxes when the declared branch is the average; the result is the declared branch value, not a classical gradient. The symmetric retained set makes the exact-real inverse-potential and force arrays real; computed enclosures retain outward bounds on any residual imaginary parts. The mesh energy is $E_{M,\mathcal K}=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k|z_k|^2$.

   If mesh-self correction is enabled, place $h_k=c_k/|D(k)|^2$ on retained residues and zero elsewhere. Apply the same normalized negative-sign tensor DFT to $h$ and multiply by $\sqrt{N_g}$ to form the real even cyclic kernel $\gamma_d=\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}h_ke^{-2\pi i\sum_rk_rd_r/M_r}$. For each particle evaluate $S_i=\sum_{\ell,m}w_\ell(t_i)w_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}$ over all support-residue pairs, retaining duplicate-wrap contributions, and set $C_M=\frac12\sum_iq_i^2(S_i-\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}c_k)$. Replace the mesh energy by $E_{M,\mathcal K}-C_M$. Replace the uncorrected force by $F_{M,i}+q_i^2\sum_{\ell,m}w_\ell(t_i)\nabla_xw_m(t_i)\gamma_{\ell-m}$, using the same derivative branch as in the preceding paragraph. This local expression differentiates both factors in $S_i$; symmetry $\gamma_d=\gamma_{-d}$ makes it equal to the derivative of $S_i/2$. It is the force gather obtained by replacing $z_k$ by $z_k-q_ib_k(t_i)$ in each retained mode. Outward enclosures include the kernel transform, local products, derivative-window factors, and subtraction.

6. Compute the finite real potential, real energy, and real force using all lattice images inside the cutoff $R$, with the energy and force excluding exactly the own zero-image term $(j,\lambda)=(i,0)$. Keep the force convention as the finite sum of differentiated retained pair kernels; do not differentiate the hard-cutoff membership indicator. Add the ordinary Ewald energy constant $-\alpha\sum_iq_i^2/\sqrt\pi$ to the total energy. The point-source potential is only returned off all source images.

7. Construct the total error ledger of
[[thm-ewald-total-pme-error-certificate]] using finite $U_3$ real and reciprocal shell controllers, every omitted mode in $\mathcal M_{K_c}$, the retained source-alias terms $A_k$, the derivative-window terms $B_k$, the mesh-self correction if enabled, and the actual outward arithmetic radii for all spread, transform, solve, gather, summation, and correction nodes. Outward enclosures for the finite controllers themselves are part of the enclosure oracle. If any required arithmetic radius or controller enclosure is unavailable, return `arithmetic-inconclusive`. Otherwise return the computed intervals and total error radii. Return `certified` when each radius meets its requested tolerance and `certified-over-tolerance` when the enclosure is valid but a tolerance is exceeded.

The analytic error statement holds for arbitrary admissible real data. Its
computable implementation requires the stated finite representation and
certified enclosures. For fixed $P$, charge spread and gather cost
$O(nP^3)$; three tensor transforms cost $O(N_g\log(2N_g))$ in the formal
operation model, plus the finite real-image count and certificate enumeration.
The optional exact self correction costs $O(N_g\log(2N_g)+nP^6)$ using a
precomputed cyclic kernel. These operation counts do not imply accuracy;
accuracy is supplied by the returned error ledger.
